rules.effective_date_basis: Starting July 1, 2024, many landlords may only charge one month's rent for unfurnished and furnished units
rules.title: Statewide security deposit cap
rules.requirement: Starting July 1, 2024, many landlords may charge no more than one month's rent as a security deposit for either unfurnished or furnished units. Landlords who own only two rental properties with no more than four residential units total may charge up to two months' rent if ownership is held by a natural person, qualifying family trust, or qualifying LLC; last month's rent counts as part of the security deposit, but first month's rent does not.
rules.key_value: 1 month's rent; qualifying small-landlord exception up to 2 months' rent

coverage.small_owner_exception: Landlords who own only two rental properties with no more than four residential units total can charge up to two months' rent if ownership is held by a natural person, family trust, or LLC where all members are natural persons.
coverage.summary: Applies to many California rental units, with a higher cap for qualifying small landlords described by ownership and portfolio size.

rules.interaction: The page states that Assembly Bill 12 changed the amount landlords can charge statewide starting July 1, 2024, and separately notes Berkeley Rent Board cannot decide whether a particular landlord may charge one or two months' rent.
rules.quoted_span:
Starting July 1, 2024, many landlords may only charge one month's rent for unfurnished and furnished units
Starting July 1, 2024, landlords who own only two rental properties with no more than four residential units total can charge up to two months' rent for furnished and unfurnished units if ownership is held by a natural person, family trust, or limited liability company (LLC) where all members are natural persons

rules.title: State security deposit deductions, inspection, documentation, and return rules
rules.requirement: Landlords must offer a walk-through inspection during the last two weeks of a tenancy, may deduct only reasonably necessary amounts for allowed purposes, and must return the remaining security deposit within 21 days after the tenant leaves the unit vacant with an itemized statement and required documentation if deductions are taken. The page also states added photo or proof requirements for certain dates: proof repairs were completed starting January 1, 2025; post-possession photographs starting April 1, 2025; and move-in photographs for tenancies beginning on or after July 1, 2025.
rules.key_value: 21 days; walk-through during last two weeks of tenancy

coverage.summary: Applies to California rental tenancies covered by the state security-deposit rules described on the page; no building age, unit-count, or owner-occupancy limit is stated.

rules.exemptions: Deductions are limited to rent default; tenant- or guest-caused damage beyond normal wear and tear; cleaning to return the unit to the same cleanliness level as at the start of the tenancy for tenancies beginning after January 1, 2003; and, if allowed by the lease, restoring or replacing personal property or furniture, excluding ordinary wear and tear.
rules.interaction: The page presents these as state-law security-deposit basics, while Berkeley's Rent Ordinance separately imposes security-deposit interest requirements for covered Berkeley units.
rules.quoted_span:
All or any remaining portion of a security deposit must be returned
within 21 days
after the tenant/s leave the unit vacant. If deductions were made, the landlord must give the tenant a written statement itemizing the amount of and and purpose for any security deposit deductions

rules.law_name: Berkeley Rent Ordinance security deposit interest requirements
rules.title: Security deposit interest for Berkeley Rent Ordinance units
rules.requirement: For tenancies in units fully or partially covered by Berkeley's Rent Ordinance, landlords must pay tenants interest on their security deposit at the end of each year and a prorated amount if the tenant moves out before year-end.
rules.key_value: Annual security-deposit interest plus prorated move-out interest

coverage.other_unresolvable: Applies only to units fully or partially covered by Berkeley's Rent Ordinance; the page does not define that coverage.
coverage.summary: Covers tenancies in units fully or partially covered by Berkeley's Rent Ordinance.

rules.interaction: The page distinguishes this Berkeley Rent Ordinance interest rule from the state-law security-deposit basics described elsewhere on the page.
rules.quoted_span: For tenancies in units fully or partially covered by Berkeley's Rent Ordinance, landlords must pay tenants interest on their security deposit at the end of each year and a prorated amount if the tenant moves out before the end of the year.
